rows.passage_en: The Sun transfers energy through space as electromagnetic radiation. Electromagnetic waves can travel across the near-vacuum between the Sun and Earth.
rows.review_note: Conduction and convection require material transport or interactions in a medium, so they do not carry heat across interplanetary space. This is a researcher interpretation of solar radiation.

rows.passage_en: Sound pressure level increases with the logarithm of pressure amplitude. Greater amplitude ordinarily gives a louder sound when other listening conditions are fixed.
rows.review_note: Loudness also depends on frequency and hearing, but amplitude is the closest of the offered basic wave properties.

rows.passage_en: A static liquid column supports a pressure difference rho*g*h, with rho its density and h the height difference.
rows.review_note: For the same pressure, a lower-density fluid requires a taller column. Water is much less dense than mercury; assume an evacuated barometer and adequate column height.

rows.passage_en: The color of an illuminated object depends on the visible wavelengths it reflects toward the observer, while other wavelengths can be absorbed.
rows.review_note: Under ordinary white illumination a red petal reflects red wavelengths. The statement is not about an object glowing by thermal emission.

rows.source_locator: uranium dating and the 4.54-billion-year age estimate
rows.passage_en: Long-lived radioactive isotopes in minerals provide clocks extending over billions of years and are used to date Earth’s early formation.
rows.review_note: Researcher inference from ancient radiometric clocks: natural radioactivity predates modern medicine and industry and was present during Earth’s formation.

rows.source_locator: paragraph beginning The most common misconception
rows.passage_en: An aircraft traveling faster than sound continuously generates the pressure waves associated with a sonic boom; it is not just a single event when passing Mach one.
rows.review_note: Supports supersonic flight rather than merely the instant of crossing the sound barrier.

rows.passage_en: For resistive components, current equals voltage divided by resistance. In a series circuit, the voltage drops add across the components.
rows.review_note: Researcher application: adding lamps in series increases total resistance and reduces current for a fixed-voltage source. Exclude current-regulated sources from this textbook idealization.

rows.passage_en: In a longitudinal wave, the medium’s particles oscillate parallel to the direction in which the disturbance propagates.
rows.review_note: For transverse waves the motion instead is perpendicular.

rows.source_locator: opening definition of a solar eclipse
rows.passage_en: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon lies between the Sun and Earth and casts its shadow onto part of Earth.
Near Earth’s surface, raising a mass through height h increases its gravitational potential energy by approximately m*g*h.
rows.review_note: Assuming a steady lift, work is about 100*9.8*2=1960 J, closest to2000J; the four seconds would be relevant to power, not total lifting work.

rows.passage_en: In special relativity, a moving object’s measured length contracts along its direction of relative motion by the factor sqrt(1-v^2/c^2).
rows.review_note: Use simultaneous length measurement in the observer frame; “appears” in the question is interpreted in this conventional sense, not a literal photograph with light-travel-time effects.

rows.source_locator: vectors and scalar-product section; researcher norm derivation
rows.passage_en: Vector addition combines components. Perpendicular vectors with magnitudes a and b have resultant magnitude sqrt(a^2+b^2).
rows.review_note: Researcher geometry: perpendicular3N and4N give5N; arbitrary angles give resultant magnitudes between1N and7N, excluding0 and8.

rows.passage_en: An electrical measuring device sensitive to current can also indicate a voltage when a known resistance relates the measured current and voltage through V=IR.
rows.review_note: Researcher calibration argument for a galvanometer and suitable resistances. It is not a claim of directly measuring arbitrary voltage with no circuit loading.

rows.source_locator: Snell-law discussion and water’s refractive-index example
rows.passage_en: For light crossing a boundary, Snell’s law relates refractive indices and angles. Total internal reflection requires an incidence angle above the critical angle.
rows.review_note: With water index about4/3 and air about1, critical angle is arcsin(3/4), about48.6degrees. At20degrees, light can pass into the air. Partial reflection can occur as well.

rows.source_locator: hydrostatic pressure relation; derived pressure-force integration
rows.passage_en: Hydrostatic pressure rises with depth. A flexible gas-filled container compresses as external pressure increases; displaced liquid volume controls its buoyancy.
rows.review_note: Researcher combination of hydrostatics, ideal-gas compression and Archimedes’ principle: an intact flexible balloon displaces less water deeper down, reducing its buoyant force. Assume no leak or rupture.

rows.passage_en: When gravity is the only force near Earth, an object accelerates downward at g regardless of whether it was released from rest or given an initial velocity.
rows.review_note: After release the hand no longer exerts a force; throwing changes initial speed, not gravitational acceleration.

rows.passage_en: For an ideal conservative force, stored potential-energy change equals the work done against that force between the initial and final states.
rows.review_note: Elastic and electrostatic energy can be present even while the objects are at rest. Assume negligible dissipative losses in storage.

rows.passage_en: Incident light may be reflected, transmitted or absorbed by matter. Absorption transfers energy into the material rather than transmitting the incident beam through it.
rows.review_note: For an opaque material transmission is negligible; reflection and absorption account for the incident energy in the intended elementary model.

rows.passage_en: The second harmonic of an ideal periodic fundamental mode has twice the fundamental frequency.
rows.review_note: The source explicitly describes the next string mode having twice the frequency.

rows.passage_en: A metal contains charges that can move in response to an electric field. These mobile charges are already part of the conducting material.
rows.review_note: The mobile carriers in copper are electrons; a current source does not need to supply all electrons originally present in the wire. Carrier identification is a researcher elementary-material interpretation.

rows.passage_en: Force and acceleration can be resolved into independent Cartesian components. If no horizontal force acts, horizontal acceleration is zero.
rows.review_note: Under ideal projectile motion without drag, the horizontal component can stay constant while vertical velocity changes under gravity.

rows.passage_en: Polarization specifies the orientation of transverse oscillations. For light, the electric-field direction lies in a plane perpendicular to propagation.
rows.review_note: A purely longitudinal displacement has no analogous choice of perpendicular vibration plane.

rows.passage_en: At fixed fluid density and gravitational acceleration, hydrostatic pressure depends on vertical depth and the pressure at the surface.
rows.review_note: The horizontal surface area does not enter p=p_surface+rho*g*h.

rows.passage_en: For a fixed mass at nonrelativistic speeds, kinetic energy is one half of mass times speed squared.
rows.review_note: Tripling speed multiplies kinetic energy by9. Since9is absent from A–C, the intended option is None of these.

rows.source_locator: equation 30.7 and discussion of grating orders
rows.passage_en: A diffraction grating superposes waves from regularly spaced openings or rulings. Their relative phases produce constructive and destructive interference.
rows.review_note: Grating maxima occur when successive wave contributions add in phase.

rows.source_locator: Z=8 oxygen and Z=10 neon rows
rows.passage_en: Atomic number counts protons and identifies the element. Removing two protons lowers atomic number by two; removing two protons and two neutrons lowers mass number by four.
rows.review_note: Neon hasZ10; after removal Z8 andA16 correspond to oxygen-16. Atomic number comes from the CIAAW table; nucleon bookkeeping is researcher arithmetic.

Electrons dominate thermal conduction in many metals, but thermal conduction in insulators is largely carried by lattice vibrations. The question does not specify a metal. Hold rather than treating the metal-specific answer as universal.

Cooling rate alone does not determine specific heat without controlling mass, surface area, emissivity, airflow and evaporation. The intended sand/vegetation comparison may rely on unstated conditions. Prefer a clearer replacement.

The location of a spectral peak depends on whether radiation is plotted per unit wavelength or per unit frequency. No curve or horizontal-axis convention is supplied. Prefer a question with an explicit convention.

Key A says microscopic slush makes water more dense. IAPWS describes ice and ice-like local structure as less dense/open. The source supports a decrease in bulk density for an ice-water mixture, not an increase. Requires independent adjudication or replacement.

note: Assumptions and researcher derivations are recorded. No question/key edits or final approvals.
